elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 3.4: "Customer may terminate this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment ... for convenience at the end of any calendar month" — the Service Option Attachments are the Order-Form-level documents under the Base Terms definition, so both agreement-level and order-level exit exist. (The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a mechanical false negative caused by the parenthetical separating "terminate this Agreement" from "for convenience"; the substance is present.)

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: 3.4(a) "providing at least one month's prior written notice to IBM" — one month is functionally the 30-day standard; the added "at the end of any calendar month" effectiveness anchor is a timing restriction rather than a longer notice period, and it is retained unchanged (favourable-to-neutral existing language).

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Neither the original nor the redlined Section 3.4 contains any refund language; the only money mechanic runs the other way (Customer pays early termination charges). To reach preferred the drafter must insert an operative sentence obliging IBM to refund prepaid charges pro rata for the period after the effective date of termination.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: IBM's only termination right in the rendered text is Section 3.3 for material breach after a 30-day cure; no IBM convenience right appears. Any Section 3.2 non-renewal mechanic is a natural-term renewal question and is evaluated under RENEWAL, not T4C.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: 3.4(a) requires only "at least one month's prior written notice," with effect at calendar month-end — an exit shorter than, and therefore more favourable than, the 60–90 day fallback ceiling. No redline needed.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Redlined 3.4(b): "paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments, not to exceed three (3) months' charges." "Charges" is the contract's own term for fees, so the cap is on the correct base and is unconditional.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: IBM has no convenience termination right at all in the rendered text (only Section 3.3 material-breach termination), which is strictly stronger than a term-end-only convenience right. The mapping's quote for this element (the Customer 3.4 right) is mis-cited, but the substantive basis holds.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: there is no IBM convenience termination right to which a notice period could attach. The mapped quote (Section 3.3 material breach) is not evidence of a convenience right; absence of the right is what satisfies the element.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: Customer's one-month convenience right beats the 60–90 day ceiling, IBM has no convenience right (so the two Vendor-side elements are satisfied by inapplicability), and the single inserted phrase supplies the missing three-month cap on early termination charges.

Preferred level remains incomplete solely because no pro-rata refund of prepaid charges is granted; to reach preferred the drafter would need to add an express IBM obligation to refund prepaid charges for the post-termination period. The comment correctly declines to pursue this rather than promising it in prose only.

Minimality holds: the edit is a seven-word tail added to Section 3.4(b) only. It deletes nothing, retains the Attachment A and Service Option Attachment cross-references, the "if any" qualifier, the calendar month-end mechanic and the Section 3.3 clawback that bars IBM from recovering 3.4(b) charges when IBM is the breaching party, and adds no survival, expense, or procedural extras.

Intent preserved: the cap operates on the same defined "early termination charges," leaves Attachment A pricing and the 3.3 cross-reference intact, and creates no undefined term, dangling reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Two mapping quotes are mis-assigned (the term-end element is quoted to Customer's 3.4 right and the 90-day element to the 3.3 breach clause). This is a citation hygiene defect only — both elements are met by the absence of any IBM convenience right — but the mapping should be corrected to cite the absence rather than an unrelated clause.

The deterministic signal "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a regex artefact (the parenthetical carve-out separates "terminate this Agreement" from "for convenience"); on inspection the Customer convenience right is plainly present in p0044 and should not be read as a coverage gap.
